purpose: Identify the factor-level cause of the different whole-model and active-NLP AutoScaler trajectories and correct the preliminary interpretation in B-M5-BAKKEN-ACTIVE-NLP-SCALING-SCREEN-001.

controls.conclusion: Matching the whole-model control's IPOPT user-scaling setting does not recover its stable trajectory.

controls.policy: active-NLP rebuild preserving inherited inequality factors
controls.conclusion: Preserving inequality factors improves the late residuals but still does not reproduce the whole-model trajectory.

source_level_cause: IDAES 2.12 AutoScaler._con_by_norm obtains a full Jacobian, enumerates an equality-only constraint list, and uses each equality-list index directly as a full-Jacobian row index. Interspersed inequalities therefore shift the row norm assigned to subsequent equalities.
interpretation: The stable whole-model AutoScaler trajectory depends on extensively misaligned equality scaling factors, not on a scientifically justified scaling policy.
The skipped non-exportable suffix warnings are not the direct trajectory switch, and preserving the 71 inequality factors is insufficient.
The preliminary statement in B-M5-BAKKEN-ACTIVE-NLP-SCALING-SCREEN-001 that the next comparison had narrowed only to inequalities and inherited factors is superseded by this factor-level result.
A corrected row-aligned scaling policy is numerically worse on this ill-conditioned model, so convergence cannot be claimed by relying on the accidental AutoScaler factor shift.
